clue.text: Why I had detectives in house?

definitions.text: Why I had detectives in house?

indicators.note: in signals that the first person and the detectives go inside the dwelling

parts.note: a house is a home
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why police detectives have descended on their home.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a killing is why detectives would be in your house. 'Why' and 'had' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A killing in the house is exactly the reason detectives would arrive, so the whole question describes the crime.

clue.text: Hospital transport needs drivers round city

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: round means the drivers' letters go around the vehicle

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation for drivers
a van is a form of transport

explanation.surface: Getting a patient to hospital requires drivers to go round the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association. 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital city of Cuba.

clue.text: Bird's coat — wow!

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
aw is an exclamation of wonder or sympathy, like wow

explanation.surface: Admiring someone's coat with an exclamation of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird's' is the definition plus a link 's; MAC is the British word for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot.

clue.text: Wagon carrying band needs off-road parking

indicators.note: carrying means the wagon word holds the band letters within it

parts.note: a cart is a wagon
the RPO is the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, a band of musicians

explanation.surface: A wagon transporting a musical group needs somewhere to park away from the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is a roofed shelter beside a house where a car is parked off the road.

clue.text: Gadget got in America — glad it converted

indicators.note: converted means these letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A tourist is pleased with a device bought in the United States after changing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got in' links the definition to the wordplay; 'converted' suggests currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital camera is a gadget for taking pictures stored electronically.

clue.text: Moments of panic as Conservative prepares to speak

parts.note: a speaker in a debate rises to his or her feet before speaking

explanation.surface: A Tory politician gets up to speak amid scenes of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: critical turning points or emergencies are moments of panic.

clue.text: Wild plant grew up on seashore

parts.note: rose means grew upwards or got higher
a bay is an inlet of the sea's shore

explanation.surface: A wild plant sprang up beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosebay willowherb is a common wildflower; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebay willowherb, known simply as rosebay, is a tall pink wildflower.

clue.text: Space in town with stage where ball may be held

parts.note: a square is an open space in a town
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: An open-air town square with a stage where a dance may be held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance; in cricket, square leg is a fielding position where a catch, holding the ball, may be taken. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Square leg is a cricket fielding position, where a fielder may hold a catch.

clue.text: Rescues dry Eliot piece

definitions.meaning: saves goods or property from loss, as from a wreck
'The Dry ...' is one of T.S. Eliot's Four Quartets

explanation.surface: Someone saves a piece of T.S. Eliot's work from boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage is to rescue, and 'The Dry Salvages' is the third of T.S. Eliot's Four Quartets.

clue.text: Give clear, new order from Mountbatten

indicators.note: a new order of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to restructure things clearly, handed down by Lord Mountbatten.
explanation.walkthrough: Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India, so anything coming from him in that office is of the viceroy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Mountbatten served as Viceroy of India, so an order from him was issued with a viceroy's authority.

clue.text: Fool in position to sniff at heavy metal?

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
being by the nose places something where it can be sniffed

explanation.surface: A fool sniffs at heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy metal' looks like rock music but is the element. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone into doing your will is to lead them by the nose.

clue.text: Pick on son in row

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the selection word after the son

parts.note: to cull is to pick out or select

explanation.surface: Someone singles out their son during a family row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel; it is the verb for rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to propel a boat with oars, which is to row.

clue.text: Poet's original career

parts.note: something original is new
to career is to rush headlong, to bolt

explanation.surface: A poet's pioneering working life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun for a job but is the verb meaning to rush. Henry Newbolt was an English poet, author of 'Drake's Drum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Newbolt was an English poet, best known for patriotic verse such as 'Vitai Lampada'.

clue.text: Einstein's province?

parts.note: read as the province belonging to Einstein, whose first name was Albert, plus an A, it names a Canadian province

explanation.surface: Asking what field of study belonged to Einstein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'province' looks like Einstein's field of expertise, but it is a Canadian province named, like Einstein, Albert with an extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian prairie province, named after Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, shares its root with Einstein's first name.

clue.text: Hornblower's new baby perhaps the right colour

parts.note: a newborn son is a little boy
blue is the colour of the political right in Britain, the Conservatives

explanation.surface: Horatio Hornblower's newborn is dressed in the correct shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Hornblower suggests C.S. Forester's naval hero, but it is the nursery-rhyme child told 'come blow your horn'. Blue is the British Conservative colour. 'perhaps' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the boy is urged 'come blow your horn', making him a literal horn blower.

clue.text: Just listen to Antony!

parts.note: Mark Antony's speech in Julius Caesar begins 'Friends, Romans, countrymen', asking his hearers for their attention

explanation.surface: Telling someone simply to listen to what Antony is saying.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Antony opens 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for listening attentively, echoing the request in Mark Antony's famous funeral oration.

clue.text: A message on board chewed: rat?

parts.note: a post is a message put up on a notice board or online forum
ate means chewed food

explanation.surface: A rat has gnawed a note pinned to a noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like the animal but means a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat, in slang, is one who deserts a cause, as an apostate abandons a faith.

clue.text: Transport not paid to St Martin's

definitions.text: Transport not paid to St Martin's

parts.words: Transport not paid to St Martin's
parts.note: in the rhyme 'Oranges and Lemons' the bells of St Martin's say 'You owe me five farthings', money still not paid, while the whole names an old bicycle

explanation.surface: A fare or delivery charge owed to a London church goes unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Oranges and Lemons' has the bells of St Martin's say 'You owe me five farthings'; a farthing was an old quarter-penny coin. The answer is the Victorian high-wheeled bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bicycle with one huge and one tiny wheel, named after a large and a small old British coin.

clue.text: Leader of herd chewing fat

indicators.note: of means the leader belongs to the herd animal, so it comes after

parts.note: the yak is a herd animal of Tibet
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: The head of a herd of cattle is chewing on some fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing the fat' is an idiom for chatting idly; 'Leader of herd' reads as king of the yaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing the fat is idle chatter, and yakking is informal for talking at length.

clue.text: Satirical speaker is one of the press?

definitions.meaning: a person who uses irony, speaking with satirical intent
jokingly, a person who presses clothes with an iron

explanation.surface: Asking whether a satirical speaker counts as a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the press' looks like journalism, but the second reading is someone who does the ironing. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ironist uses irony, and whimsically one who irons, pressing clothes.

clue.text: Topping suitable for vegetarian?

parts.note: topping means a hat, and a vegetarian might eat pulses, so the hat's name sounds like a legume-based item

explanation.surface: Asking which pizza topping would suit a vegetarian diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' suggests food on a pizza, but it is headwear; the hat's name begins with a pulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A small close-fitting knitted hat, which sits on top of the head.

clue.text: Flashpoint as big beast turns to fight

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as in boxing practice

indicators.note: turns means the name of the big animal is read backwards

parts.note: the elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A tense moment when a huge animal wheels round to do battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flashpoint' looks like a moment of crisis, but a sparkle is a point of flashing light. The indicator 'turns' reverses only the beast; 'as' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkle is a glinting point of light, a tiny flash, so the clue word fits as a point that flashes.

clue.text: Showing muscle, energy, and heart to secure high honour

parts.note: E is the physics abbreviation for energy

indicators.note: to secure means the heart word holds the honour inside it

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
CH is the Companion of Honour, a high British award

explanation.surface: A display of strength, energy and courage earns someone a top award.
explanation.walkthrough: An écorché is an anatomical figure drawn or modelled with the skin removed, showing the muscles. CH (Companion of Honour) is a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word means flayed: an écorché figure shows the body's muscles with no skin over them.

clue.text: Scale from top of crocodile leg

indicators.note: top of, in a down clue, picks the first letter of crocodile

parts.note: a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: Some scales taken from the upper part of a crocodile's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks like a reptile's scale, but it is the verb meaning to climb. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or mountain is to climb it.

clue.text: Caucasian is a nobody — well, almost one

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for nobody is dropped

parts.note: a nobody is a zero, a person of no account
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone from the Caucasus is dismissed as a nonentity, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ZERO to ZER; 'well' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Azeri is a native of Azerbaijan, a country in the Caucasus region.

clue.text: Removal of a benefit fired one up inside

indicators.note: up inside means the fired and one words sit within the benefit word

parts.note: a boon is a benefit or blessing
fired, as of a fire or lamp, means lit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone loses a state benefit after a firing and is fired up inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Abolition is the doing away with something, its removal, as of slavery or a tax.

clue.text: Make wild area into new green

indicators.note: into means the area letter goes inside the rearranged letters
new means the letters of green are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A plan to rewild some land by turning it into a new green space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns GREEN into ENRGE; A goes inside after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to madden or infuriate someone is to make them wild with anger.

clue.text: Have four legs and flat top? That's not necessarily best

definitions.text: Have four legs and flat top?
definitions.meaning: something with four legs and a flat top would be a piece of furniture
something that can be defeated is not necessarily the best

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture is told it will never be the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical description of being a table; split as BE A TABLE it gives the letters. 'That's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being defeated is not necessarily the best, since it can still be bettered.
